What are your thoughts on the current policy and do you think that it will be effective in creating new communities, or will it isolate existing ones?

Personally, I don't think it's very healthy to just give a subverse to the first person who happened to load voat first. There are plenty of existing communities wishing to migrate over to voat (yes, I'm talking about reddit), who are finding their community name already taken by people wishing to intentionally hijack their name and the reputation that they've built.

There is of course /v/subverserequest, and whilst it's far better than reddit's system, I think it needs to be greatly improved before communities that wish to migrate give up because their default name has been hijacked. By the term hijacked, I don't mean another group has tried to start their own similar community, but rather a group of people dedicated to ruining it ( /v/ukraine for example).

I'm not saying that mods from subreddits on reddit in particular should have first pick at the equivalent subverse, that would be terrible! Rather that everyone should be given an equal opportunity to contest a subverse registration within a given time, allowing them to provide information to the community regarding their plans on how they intend to run that community. The community as a whole can then judge on who they want to control the subverse by way of a democratic vote.
A discussion about the "first-come, first-served" policy of registering subverses.

Although I see the concern, placing subverses in purgatory for whatever length of time it takes to decide who gets to mod them is going to stifle the development of Voat until the time has expired and people have voted on who should be in control of the subverse. This would also require the development of some sort of voting system which would take a while further extending the purgatory for subverses. Also, how do we decide which subverses are free to claim and which ones you need to be elected for to create?

TL;DR: People stealing subs to ruin them are dicks. I don't know what to do about it though.

If I remember correctly, Reddit was this way at the beginning too.

I don't think there's any other way to do it. Subverse request has to be the best option. With Voat's open community, if a group wants to take a subverse to hate on a group of people, they can. That was part of the FPH deal. Yes, it's annoying, yes, it's insulting, but we can't really complain about it.

Generally speaking, I don't think preferential treatment should be given to Reddit communities over someone who was here first. Just because they were mods on Reddit shouldn't mean they get to be mods here. A lot of people here were fed up with many of the Reddit mods.

But, I would be in favor of preferential treatment being given to actual communities over some guy just sitting on the sub not doing much, just taking it to be a jerk.

That all said, is it a situation where there's a sub that matches the name of the one you had on Reddit but you don't really want to post on the one here because you're not a mod and don't want to contribute and participate unless you can also moderate? If there is a community here, I would just suggest posting there and contributing rather than trying to migrate Reddit's entrenched power hierarchy over here. I'm not saying you specifically are doing that, but in general terms, I imagine that situation is going to be popping up once in a while.

I don't think something like that would be useful for smaller niche subreddits where the sole mod is pretty much single-handedly holding everything together, but I could see such a system working well for some subs.
